NH homestead right protects $400,000 of a person's homestead (or interest in it) from creditors (asset-protection, not a property tax exemption).
To claim it the residence must have been a primary residence continuously for the previous 12 months; sale proceeds are protected if reinvested within 6 months in a new primary residence.
The homestead right does not erase debt; it is exempt from levy or sale on execution except in listed cases, including collection of taxes.

Property tax elderly exemption requires 3 consecutive years of NH residence before April 1, and income and asset limits set by the town or city, no lower than $13,400 single / $20,400 married income and $35,000 net assets.

claim: A municipality that adopted the lien procedure may lien real estate if taxes are not paid by December 1 after assessment.
Collector must give notice at least 30 days before executing the lien, by certified or registered mail to the owner.
Redemption: any person with a legal interest may redeem before a deed is given by paying the lien amount with interest at 14 percent per annum plus costs.
Only the municipality, county or state may acquire a tax lien on land and buildings.
After 2 years from execution of the lien the collector executes a deed to the lienholder for unredeemed land.
After 2 years from execution of an unredeemed real estate tax lien, the collector executes a tax deed to the lienholder.
A municipality may refuse a tax deed; the lien then remains indefinitely and the right of redemption continues with interest.
Redemption at 14 percent per annum is available until a deed is given.
Under the older tax sale procedure the collector deeds to the purchaser after 2 years from the sale.
A collector's deed for property purchased at a tax sale is exempt from the transfer tax.
For residential tenancies, 30 days' eviction notice suffices; 7 days if the reason is nonpayment, substantial damage, behavior affecting health/safety, or domestic violence cotenant termination.
Notice must state the reason with specificity; nonpayment notices must advise of the right to cure under RSA 540:9.

Restricted property may be terminated only for listed reasons including nonpayment, substantial damage, material lease violation, other good cause, and lease expiration with 60 days' notice for leases of 12 months or longer.
After the notice expires the landlord obtains a landlord-tenant writ; the return day is 7 days from service; if the tenant appears a hearing is set within 10 days.
cite: Navigating the NH Eviction Process | NH Judicial Branch

claim: Tenant may cure nonpayment by paying back rent plus $15, up to three times in 12 months; money judgments in these cases are limited to $1500.
